card.name: Linking words after "in combination"
card.fires_on: The small linking word right after a combination phrase, mainly "with" in "in combination with", also "and" or "plus" joining a drug to its partner drug. Seen in oncology dosing and indication text.

modes.label: "with" after "in combination"
modes.description: The word "with" that follows "in combination" and comes just before the partner drug.
modes.example: Administer OPDIVO in combination<< with>> fluoropyrimidine- and platinum‑

modes.label: "and" or "plus" joining co-treatments
modes.description: A joining word that links a drug to another drug or to radiation therapy in a regimen.

card.writes: It suppresses words meaning combine or combination, so the next word is less likely to repeat the idea and more likely to name the partner drug.
card.plain: It fires on the little word that links one cancer drug to its partner, as in "in combination with".
